ggplot2: geom_point()

Our tutorial will look at the pie_crab dataset provided by the lterdatasampler package. Let’s start by loading it into R.

If you haven’t already, you will need to download the package. Run the following code in your console to install the package. There are a couple other packages that will be needed for this tutorial.

install.packages('lterdatasampler')
install.packages('ggplot2')

Now that you have installed the package, you will need to load it in order to gain access to the datasets. Do this using the library() function. Put this at the top of your script, along with any other packages you want to use.

library(lterdatasampler)
library(ggplot2)

Now that the pacakge is loaded, we can get our data using the data() function. This will create an object called pie_crab that will now be in our global environment.

data("pie_crab")

geom_point() draws one dot per row of your data. Choose which columns go on each axis and optionally colour the dots by a third column.

viewof x = Inputs.select(["size", "air_temp", "air_temp_sd", "water_temp", "water_temp_sd"], {label: "X axis"})
viewof y = Inputs.select(["size", "air_temp", "air_temp_sd", "water_temp", "water_temp_sd"], {label: "Y axis"})
viewof color = Inputs.select(["size", "air_temp", "air_temp_sd", "water_temp", "water_temp_sd"], {label: "Colour by"})
rows = transpose(choices)
match = rows.find(d => d.x === x && d.y === y && d.color === color)
{
if (!match) {
const p = document.createElement("p");
p.textContent = "Pick two different columns for X and Y.";
return p;
}
const img = document.createElement("img");
img.src = match.image;
img.style.maxWidth = "100%";
return img;
}

The code that made this plot:

{
const pre = document.createElement("pre");
pre.className = "plot-code";
const code = document.createElement("code");
code.textContent = match ? match.code : "";
pre.appendChild(code);
return pre;
}
